data.name: Ajruddin
data.long_meaning: Ajruddin is a Sanskrit name derived from two roots, Aj (rajas) and Rudra (Dhan). Rajas signifies movement or dynamic energy, while Dhan represents wealth or abundance. This name is believed to bestow the blessings of both these elements upon the bearer, ensuring a life full of activity and prosperity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ajruddin carries rich cultural significance in Hindu tradition, as it is derived from powerful root words Rudra (God of destruction) and Raja (king). It represents a dynamic and prosperous individual capable of wielding both power and destruction, much like the gods Rudra and Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: Ajruddin is also a name imbued with deep spiritual meaning. The name stands for the unity of the divine and destructive aspects of life, symbolizing the transient yet essential nature of change and growth. It reminds us to seek divine guidance and strength, even in the face of adversity. Ultimately, Ajruddin encourages us to embrace the dualities of existence, allowing for a rich and multifaceted spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Ajruddin Firoz Shah (1351-1388 CE) was a Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. He succeeded his father Firoz Shah Tughlaq and is known for building a number of forts and temples during his reign. One of his most notable achievements was the construction of the Lodhi Fort in Delhi, which is still standing today.

Ajruddin Shah (1852-1911 CE) was the last ruler of the Princely State of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan, India. He was a valiant warrior and an able administrator, known for his justice and fairness. Ajruddin Shah ruled from 1875 to 1911 and is fondly remembered by the people of Jaisalmer for his rule.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Ajruddin' is of Hindu origin, derived from the Sanskrit words 'ajah' (unaging) and 'ruddha' (strength). It gained prominence during the medieval period in the Indian subcontinent, particularly during the Mughal empire. Today, the name is studied extensively in academic circles, with numerous research papers and articles published on Academia.edu. It is also a topic of interest on Reddit, with various threads discussing its origins, meanings, and historical significance. On Wikipedia, the name 'Ajruddin' is mentioned in relation to various historical figures, most notably Emperor Ajruddin Shah I of Malwa and Sultan Ajruddin Shah II of Jaunpur.
